doc.title: Jerry Hey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 2, 2023

title: Al Jarreau's Breaking Away: the players and the late-night sessions
summary: Hey lists likely keyboard and guitar players on the Jarreau record with Jay Graydon producing; horns started near eleven at night.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: When you read the minutiae about certain recordings I’m amazed that like Al Jarreau song “Breaking Away” I was just reading the minutiae about this and you know they had eight keyboard players and two guitars and two basses and horns and recorded in three or four different studios. I don’t have a question there but it’s amazing.

Well different keyboard players on different songs so you know George Duke I’m sure played on some things and there’s a guy who played in Al’s band for a long time, Tom Canning, I’m sure he was playing. Probably David Foster. Who else? I’m not sure but you know, and then the guitar players would be Jay Graydon of course, who is the producer, an excellent guitar player. Steve Lukather played on some things. Probably maybe Larry Carlton or Greg Parker depending on what the song called for. But you know that’s kind of standard. And Jay was the producer on that so you know he’s kind of the overseer on everything. So it’s going to all sound, because it’s Jay, it’s going to all sound like one unit.

Yeah he had a great thing going on with those rhythm guitars and a certain kind of effect on them was really distinctive. I understand he liked to start his studio sessions like at midnight or something.

Yeah. All the Jarreau horn parts were — I don’t think we played a note before eleven maybe, and we would finish at six or seven in the morning. And on the Jarreau record we had already been booked during the day. You know the movie calls come out a month
